introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information and Communication Technologies (0796), Paper 3 (practical), June 2026. Duration: two hours. Answer ALL TASKS.**

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group 1, Group 2 and Group 3 (booklets 00/0796/3/G1, G2 and G3). Each version has two tasks, Task A (Databases, 28 marks) and Task B (Spreadsheet, 22 marks), on the same model, with different files, names, weights and cell references.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is require to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

The working files (the database and the workbook of each group) are supplied on the day in the Candidate folder; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Determine the following table elements after normalization.

Primary keys: ................................

Foreign key: ................................

Composite keys: ................................

Table containing composite keys: ................................  *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three tables are **Employee** (StaffNo, Surname, First_Name, Department, Age, Absence), **Emp_Salary** (Staff_No, Dept_ID, Salary) and **Department** (Dept_ID, Department). Reading them one by one:

- **Primary keys:** `StaffNo` (table Employee: one value per member of staff) and `Dept_ID` (table Department: one value per department).
- **Foreign key:** in Emp_Salary, `Staff_No` (it refers to Employee.StaffNo) and `Dept_ID` (it refers to Department.Dept_ID). A foreign key is a field that is the primary key of another table and that links the two tables.
- **Composite key:** (`Staff_No`, `Dept_ID`): neither field alone identifies a row of Emp_Salary (an employee may be paid in several departments and a department pays many employees), but the pair does.
- **Table containing the composite key:** **Emp_Salary**. It is the link (junction) table between Employee and Department, and its two key fields are at the same time foreign keys.

Marking idea (4 marks): primary keys (1), foreign key (1), composite key (1), table (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Create a relationship between the three tables.

Take a screen capture of the active relationship window.

Open the Word document *My Screen shots* in your candidate folder and paste your screen capture.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Creating the relationships.** Close all the tables, then *Database Tools* > *Relationships*. In *Show Table* add **Employee**, **Emp_Salary** and **Department**, then *Close*.

1. Drag `StaffNo` of **Employee** onto `Staff_No` of **Emp_Salary**. In *Edit Relationships* tick *Enforce Referential Integrity* and click *Create*: Access draws a one-to-many line (1 at Employee, the infinity sign at Emp_Salary).
2. Drag `Dept_ID` of **Department** onto `Dept_ID` of **Emp_Salary**, tick *Enforce Referential Integrity* and click *Create* (one-to-many again).
3. The relationship window now shows the three tables joined by two lines. Save the layout (Ctrl+S).

```
+------------------+ 1        N +-------------------+ N        1 +------------------+
| Employee         |------------| Emp_Salary        |------------| Department       |
|------------------|            |-------------------|            |------------------|
| StaffNo (PK)     |            | Staff_No (PK, FK) |            | Dept_ID (PK)     |
| Surname          |            | Dept_ID  (PK, FK) |            | Department       |
| ...              |            | Salary            |            +------------------+
+------------------+            +-------------------+
```

Reading: one employee can have several lines in Emp_Salary, and one department appears in many lines; Emp_Salary resolves the many-to-many link between employees and departments.

**Screen capture.** With the relationship window showing, press *Print Screen* (or use the Snipping Tool to select the window). Open **My Screen shots** from the Candidate folder in Word, click where the picture must go and paste it (Ctrl+V). Save the Word document (Ctrl+S).

Marking idea (3 marks): the two relationships created with the right fields (2); the screen capture pasted in My Screen shots (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) Create a query that selects the records of employees who are older than 45 years and have salaries between 225000 and 415000. Display only the fields *Surname, Age, Salary* and *Department*. Save the query as ***First_Selection***.

Describe what you have done in the filtering criteria in the lines below

................................

................................

................................  *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Design of the query.** *Create* > *Query Design*; in *Show Table* add **Employee** and **Emp_Salary** (the relationship of question 4 joins `StaffNo` to `Staff_No`). Double-click the four fields to bring them into the grid:

| Field | Surname | Age | Salary | Department |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Table | Employee | Employee | Emp_Salary | Employee |
| Show | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Criteria | | >45 | Between 225000 And 415000 | |

**Description of the filtering criteria** (what to write on the lines):

- In the *Criteria* row of the field **Age** I typed `>45`: "older than 45" means strictly more than 45, so a person aged exactly 45 is not selected.
- In the *Criteria* row of the field **Salary** I typed `Between 225000 And 415000` (the same as `>=225000 And <=415000`): both limits are included.
- The two criteria are on the **same** *Criteria* row, so they are joined by AND: a record is displayed only if it satisfies both conditions.
- Only Surname, Age, Salary and Department have the *Show* box ticked. I ran the query, then saved it with Ctrl+S under the name **First_Selection**.

Check (invented data run in SQLite, not from the paper): with ages 50, 46, 45, 52, 30, 61, 47 and salaries 300000, 225000, 415000, 415000, 250000, 520000, 224999, the query keeps exactly the employees aged 50 (300000), 46 (225000) and 52 (415000): age 45 is excluded by `>45`, the salary 415000 is included, 520000 and 224999 are excluded.

Marking idea (5 marks): the two tables used (1); the four fields displayed (1); criterion on Age (1); criterion on Salary (1); the query saved under the right name (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) Switch to the *SQL View* and copy the code of your query. Paste the SQL code in *My Screen shots* Word document.  *[1 mark]*

**Print a copy of the My Screen shots.**
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the *Home* (or *Design*) tab click *View* > **SQL View**. Access shows the statement it wrote for the design grid:

```sql
SELECT Employee.Surname, Employee.Age, Emp_Salary.Salary, Employee.Department
FROM Employee INNER JOIN Emp_Salary ON Employee.StaffNo = Emp_Salary.Staff_No
WHERE (((Employee.Age)>45) AND ((Emp_Salary.Salary) Between 225000 And 415000));
```

Select all the text (Ctrl+A), copy it (Ctrl+C), open the Word document **My Screen shots** and paste it (Ctrl+V). Save the document and print it (*File* > *Print*).

Reading of the statement: `SELECT` lists the four fields displayed; `FROM ... INNER JOIN ... ON` joins the two tables through StaffNo and Staff_No; `WHERE` holds the two criteria (Age above 45 AND Salary between the two limits). The statement was run in SQLite on the invented data of question 7a and gave the expected three rows (Access adds the extra brackets; they do not change the meaning).

Marking idea (1 mark): SQL code of the query pasted in the document.
